summary: Loader stub disguised as `buffer` side-loads sibling scoped package on require
details: @sqlite-labs/nodesql ships a verbatim copy of the feross/buffer library under an unrelated scope, with a single added top-level statement in index.js: `var ins = import('@sqlite-labs/createsql');`. Any consumer that `require()`s this package triggers a dynamic import of the sibling scoped package `@sqlite-labs/createsql`, whose code then executes in the installer's process. The disguise is reinforced by packaging mismatches: the package name (`@sqlite-labs/nodesql`) does not match the shipped source (buffer), the description is empty, and the README's install instructions and title reference unrelated names (`@sql-access/nods`, `bare-stream`). The loader-stub shape (repackaged popular library + one-line side-load of a lookalike scoped sibling) delivers arbitrary code from the sibling package to any downstream consumer at require time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
